note.label: 1 Samuel 26: David Spares Saul a Second Time

precepts.why:
“Then came up the Ziphites to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself with us in strong holds in the wood, in the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of Jeshimon? Now therefore, O king, come down according to all the desire of thy soul to come down; and our part shall be to deliver him into the king’s hand.”

Right here we are going back: chapter 26 picks this thread back up. Again “the Ziphites came unto Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, which is before Jeshimon?”

And again Saul went down “to the wilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel with him.” “But David abode in the wilderness”, and he “sent out spies, and understood that Saul was come in very deed.”

points: When the Ziphites offered to deliver David up, Saul blessed them and sent them back: go, prepare yet, and know and see his place where his haunt is, and who hath seen him there, and come ye again to me with the certainty.

Saul is asking the Ziphites for intel. He knows David is a man of war, and he wants to be absolutely sure David is exactly where they say he is before he comes down; for it was told him that David dealeth very subtilly.
